newsitem.title: JAPAN: JNOC signs oil survey pact with Kazakhstan.
newsitem.headline: JNOC signs oil survey pact with Kazakhstan.

text.p: State-owned Japan National Oil Corp (JNOC) said on Friday it had signed a fresh agreement with Kazakhstan to conduct a seismic survey and test drilling in two separate areas northwest of the Aral Sea.

An exploration well will be drilled over a two-year period in a project area northwest of the Aral Sea based on previous seismic studies. The project is estimated to cost two billion yen, a JNOC official said.
Seismic studies will be conducted and an exploration well drilled over a period of five years in the Teresken project area at a cost of five billion to seven billion yen.
The two areas are believed to have estimated oil reserves of 500 million barrels each, JNOC said.
On Friday, an optional production sharing agreement was also signed between Japan JIT Oil (Kazakhstan) Co Ltd and Kazakhstan's energy ministry.
The parties concerned will decide whether to go ahead with the agreement after they have studied the results of their exploration tests.
Japan JIT is owned equally by Japan Petroleum Exploration Co Ltd, Teikoku Oil Co Ltd and Indonesia Petroleum Ltd, with each company having a 33.3 percent interest.
Last September, JNOC signed a deal to spend over $50 million prospecting for oil offshore in Kazakhstan.
At the time, JNOC president Kunio Komatsu told a news conference in Almaty that the company eventually hoped to produce oil from Kazakhstan's resource-rich Caspian Sea shelf.
JNOC has been conducting seismic studies in the area since an agreement was signed in April 1994.
